sources.entry: Snappy - Open-source, Ubuntu-style screenshot tool with an adjustable selection, window and full-screen capture, markup, blur, and text copying. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/beqaabu/Snappy) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Snappy
summary.one_liner: Snappy is an open-source, Ubuntu-style screenshot tool for macOS that freezes the screen so you can adjust, mark up, and copy a capture with one shortcut.
use_cases: Capture a region of the screen and adjust it before saving
Mark up screenshots with arrows, boxes, and numbered steps
Blur tokens or private details before sharing a screenshot
Copy error messages or text from images and videos
Capture a single window or open menus with a timer
summary.what_it_does: Snappy is a macOS menu bar app bound to a shortcut (⌘⇧2 by default). After you drag a selection, the screen freezes so you can move and resize the area and then annotate it with arrows, boxes, pen, highlighter, text, numbered steps, and blur. Pressing ⌘C on a selection copies the text in it, and QR codes copy their link; the page says recognition runs on the Mac. Captures are saved to ~/Pictures/Screenshots and copied to the clipboard by default, and a preview appears in the corner for dragging into other apps. Window capture on hover, full-screen capture, and a 3-second timer are also offered.
notable: Ubuntu-style selection, window, and screen capture flow with a frozen screen
Copy text from a selection, including text in images and videos, processed on-device
Blur pixelates in the saved image
MIT licensed, no account, no analytics
caveats: Requires Screen Recording permission on macOS
Not notarized by Apple, so macOS needs manual approval via Open Anyway
Homebrew 6+ requires trusting the third-party tap
